_schema.about: XPerf's own performance table for the 82 GA / turboprop / business-jet types previously read from EUROCONTROL. Built from independent public sources only (manufacturer pages and brochures, POH/AFM figures, magazine standard-data pages, compiled reference pages); EUROCONTROL data was used only as a private sanity check and is not copied here. For flight simulation only — not for real-world flight planning.
_schema.generated_by: tools/build_ga_perf.py (edit there, then regenerate); validate with tools/validate_ga_perf.py

value_object.v: the value, in the unit listed under perf_fields
value_object.ref: what the source says, in its own units/conditions
value_object.method: for der/est: how the value was derived or estimated (rule ids in [brackets], see rules)

status.pub: published figure, read online from the cited source on checked_on (directly or via a search engine's summary of that page)
status.rec: published figure attributed to the cited document, from recall, NOT re-read online — verify before release

perf_fields.takeOffDistance: m — pistons/turboprops: total distance to 50 ft (15 m) at MTOW, SL, ISA, paved dry; jets: take-off field length (FAR/CS-25) at MTOW, SL, ISA. Note: EUROCONTROL's value for GA types is closer to a ground roll, so runway checks get more conservative
perf_fields.takeOffV2: kt IAS — pistons/turboprops: speed at 50 ft; jets: V2
perf_fields.initialClimbIAS: kt IAS — climb speed below 5,000 ft (Vy for pistons)
perf_fields.initialClimbROC: fpm — sea-level climb rate at MTOW
perf_fields.climb150IAS: kt IAS — climb speed 5,000 ft–FL150 (turboprops, jets)
perf_fields.climb240IAS: kt IAS — climb speed FL150–FL240 (pressurized turboprops, jets)
perf_fields.cruiseTAS: kt TAS at the power/altitude in the type's cruise block (not necessarily 65%)
perf_fields.cruiseCeiling: hundreds of ft — service ceiling (pistons) or maximum operating/certified altitude (turboprops, jets)
perf_fields.cruiseRange: NM — published maximum range (conditions in ref)
perf_fields.approachIAS: kt IAS — speed flown in the last 1,500/2,000/3,000 ft AGL (piston/turboprop/jet)
perf_fields.landingVat: kt IAS — threshold / approach speed at 50 ft (Vref)
perf_fields.landingDistance: m — pistons/turboprops: total distance from 50 ft at max landing weight, SL, ISA; jets: unfactored landing distance (conditions in ref)

other_fields.engine: count, kind, fuel (avgas | jet-a), turbocharged, diesel, pressurized, and per-engine power: hp (shaft/brake hp) or thrustKN — replaces EUROCONTROL power-plant text parsing and ENGINE_FIX
other_fields.wingspan_m: m — used by the jet drag polar
other_fields.cruise: power setting and altitude that cruiseTAS refers to (null = not stated by the source)
other_fields.fuel.cruise: published cruise fuel flow: kgh (kg/h, total for all engines), with setting / alt_ft / tas_kt; avgas 2.72 kg/US gal, Jet A 3.04 kg/US gal or 0.803 kg/L
other_fields.sourcing_reasons: why a type is graded weak
other_fields.sourcing: good: all core values (MTOW, cruise TAS, ceiling, TO/LDG distance, climb rate, engine power) published by the manufacturer or in the POH and checked online; fair: core values sourced but partly secondary or recalled; weak: some core value estimated, aggregator-only, or more than two recalled

rules.VAT: landingVat ≈ 1.3 × Vso (published landing-configuration stall speed); the FAR/CS-23 VREF definition
rules.V50: takeOffV2 (speed at 50 ft) ≈ 1.2 × Vso; FAR/CS-23 minimum speed at 50 ft is 1.2 × VS1
rules.VY: initialClimbIAS ≈ 1.55 × Vso (Vy/Vso ratio of the C172S 1.54 and C182T 1.63 from their POHs)
rules.APP: approachIAS ≈ 1.5 × Vso, rounded to 5 kt (flaps-up/initial approach; C172S POH gives 65–75 KIAS = 1.35–1.56 Vso)
rules.APPJ: approachIAS ≈ Vref + 40 kt (speed typically flown ~3,000 ft AGL before final flap)
rules.APPROD: approachROD ≈ 5.3 × approachIAS (3° glide path: fpm ≈ 101.3 × kt × tan 3°), rounded to 50
rules.DESIAS: descentIAS ≈ the larger of cruise IAS (cruise TAS / (1 + 0.02 × cruise altitude in thousands of ft)) and 0.75 × cruise TAS, rounded to 5 kt — high-flying turboprops/turbo pistons descend faster than their cruise IAS
rules.DESIASJ: descentIAS: 250 KIAS for light jets (MTOW ≤ 7,000 kg, Vmo ≈ 260–280), 280 KIAS otherwise (typical business-jet descent schedule)
rules.DESROD: descentROD by class: 500 fpm unpressurized piston (the descent-chart assumption in Piper/Mooney POHs), 1,000 fpm pressurized piston or unpressurized turboprop, 1,500 fpm pressurized turboprop, 2,500 fpm jet
rules.JCLIMB: jet climb schedule: initial climb 200 KIAS, 250 KIAS to FL150 and FL240 (ICAO/FAA 250 kt limit below FL100, commonly held to the Mach transition), Mach climb at cruise Mach − 0.05
rules.JROC: jet climb rates as fractions of the sea-level climb rate: 0.8 to FL150, 0.5 to FL240, 0.25 above FL240 — calibrated so the Citation XLS Gen2 (4,400 fpm est. at SL) reproduces Textron's published 26 min direct climb to FL430
rules.JROC0: jet sea-level climb rate ≈ 10,600 fpm × (total thrust / MTOW); ratio calibrated on the published rates of the CJ3 Gen3 (4,478), M2 Gen2 (3,698) and HondaJet Elite II (4,100)
rules.TPCLIMB: turboprop cruise-climb IAS ≈ 1.3 × initialClimbIAS; climb rate 0.85 × sea-level rate to FL150 and 0.65 × to FL240 (flat-rated PT6/TPE331 power holds into the mid-teens)
rules.V2J: takeOffV2 ≈ Vref + 5 kt (V2 at MTOW ≈ 1.13 VSR in take-off flap; Vref = 1.23 VSR at the lower landing weight)
rules.VREFJ: Vref at typical landing weight as reported in public pilot reports / operator data for the type; ±10 kt
rules.RANGE: cruiseRange ≈ 4.5 h × cruise TAS (typical full-fuel endurance less reserve for GA types); no published range found
rules.TOGR: takeOffDistance (to 50 ft) ≈ ground roll × 1.7 (pistons) or × 1.4 (turboprops) — ratios of sourced types in this table (C172S 1.70, C182T 1.90, T206H 1.86, C23 1.73; King Air 260 1.23, Grand Caravan EX 1.54)
rules.LDGGR: landingDistance (from 50 ft) ≈ ground roll × 2.3 (pistons) or × 1.8 (turboprops) — ratios of sourced types in this table (C172S 2.32, C182T 2.29, T206H 1.90, C23 2.11; King Air 260 1.63, Grand Caravan EX 1.83)
rules.MACH: cruiseMACH = cruise TAS / 573.6 kt (speed of sound at or above 36,089 ft ISA) unless a cruise altitude is stated
rules.TAS: cruiseTAS = cruise Mach × 573.6 kt (ISA at or above 36,089 ft)
rules.WTC: wtc from MTOW: L ≤ 7,000 kg, M above (ICAO Doc 8643 wake categories)
rules.DESIG: type designator description from the engine count and kind: L<n>P/T/J (landplane)
